title: "The R Package"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`quartifyr` is a single installable R package: `render_report()` runs the
full two-pass pipeline (Quarto shell render → `reportifyr` fill) in one
call. `reportifyr` and `pyro` are pulled straight from
`a2-ai.r-universe.dev` since neither has a CRAN release. The Python
engine behind `styling_*()` (docx generation/layout) is bundled inside
the package (`inst/python/`) and called via a `pyro` bridge rather than
reimplemented in R -- see `vignette("architecture")` for the two-pass
split this reflects. The package itself is **not** `renv`-managed (no
`renv.lock` at the package root); install it into each report project's
own `renv` library explicitly.

This is a convenience wrapper, not a requirement: `render_report()`
chains `quarto render`, `styling_apply_layout()`, and
`reportifyr::build_report()` together and adopts a specific
`report/shell`/`report/draft`/`report/final` directory convention. See
`vignette("architecture")`'s "Using the pieces directly" section for
calling the three pieces yourself instead.

## Setup

```r
# Install the package into a report project's own renv library, run from
# that project's directory
renv::install("jprybylski/quartifyr")

# Provision the project's quartifyr Python dependency group (once per
# project, alongside reportifyr::initialize_report_project())
quartifyr::initialize_quartifyr_project(getwd())

# Install the Quarto extension into the project
quartifyr::install_quartifyr_extension()
```

See `vignette("installation")`.

## Usage

As an R function:

```r
library(quartifyr)

result <- render_report(
  shell_qmd = "/path/to/project/report.qmd",
  status = "draft"   # or "final"
)
# result$shell, result$draft, result$final (NULL unless status == "final")
```

`examples/*/render.R` is a thin CLI wrapper around the same call:

```bash
Rscript render.R
Rscript render.R --final
```

<img src="../man/figures/render-pipeline.gif" alt="Terminal recording of Rscript render.R running the full two-pass pipeline on the demo report, then Rscript render.R --final, producing report/draft and report/final docx files" width="700" loading="lazy">

`shell_qmd` lives at the project root alongside `_extensions/`. The
project's `_quarto.yml` must set `project: {output-dir: report/shell}`,
since `reportifyr::make_doc_dirs()` derives `report/draft/` and
`report/final/` output paths by substring-replacing "shell" in the
*rendered docx's* containing directory, not the qmd's, so this is
load-bearing, not just a naming convention.

## What `render_report()` actually does

1. Checks `check_quarto_extensions()` against `quartifyr_quarto_extensions`
   (currently just `A2-ai/quarto-plus`), erroring with a clickable
   `quarto::quarto_add_extension()` suggestion if a required one is
   missing -- before spending time rendering into a failure Quarto itself
   reports far less specifically.
2. Regenerates `abbreviations.tex` next to `shell_qmd` from the
   project's `standard_footnotes.yaml`, via `styling_build_abbreviations_tex()`.
3. Renders `shell_qmd` with Quarto against a docx reference-doc --
   whichever `reference_doc` you pass explicitly; failing that, whatever
   the `.qmd`'s frontmatter or the project's `_quarto.yml` already
   configures; failing that, the package's own bundled
   `inst/templates/org-reference.docx` -- passing `-M
   document-status:DRAFT` or `:FINAL` depending on `status`.
4. Runs `styling_apply_layout()` on the rendered shell.
5. Runs `reportifyr::build_report()` to fill in tables/figures/footnotes
   from `OUTPUTS/`, producing `report/draft/<name>-draft.docx`.
6. When `status = "final"`, also runs `reportifyr::finalize_document()`,
   producing `report/final/<name>-final.docx`.
7. Optionally (`resolve_same_page_crossrefs = TRUE`, default off), runs
   `styling_resolve_same_page_crossrefs()` on each produced docx.
8. Optionally (`recalculate_fields = TRUE`, default off), runs
   `styling_recalculate_fields()` on each produced docx.

See `vignette("styling")` for what each of those `styling_*()` calls
does on its own.

## Front matter: `validate_header()` and `header_helper()`

A quartifyr shell `.qmd` carries a lot of frontmatter -- title/memo,
signature page, synopsis, appendices, page header/footer, ... (see
`vignette("quarto-extension")`). Both functions below are driven by one
shared, in-package field registry (every field either filter actually
reads, with its requiredness and a one-line description), so they stay
in sync with the extension itself rather than with separately maintained
documentation -- run either one to see the current, authoritative field
list instead of looking it up here.

`validate_header()` checks a shell `.qmd` (and its project's
`_quarto.yml`) against that registry and prints what's provided, what's
missing, what else is available, and any conflicts (`title:`/`memo:`
both set, an unresolvable `header-format:` placeholder, an unrecognized
`crossref-hyperlinks:` value, a `logo:`/`bibliography:` path that
doesn't exist on disk, ...):

```r
quartifyr::validate_header("report.qmd")
```

Pass `strict = TRUE` to abort (rather than just print) when something
required is missing or a conflict was found -- useful as a pre-render
gate in a script. `quiet = TRUE` suppresses the printed report and just
returns the structured result (`ok`, `provided`, `missing_required`,
`missing_recommended`, `available`, `problems`) for programmatic use.

`header_helper()` is the other direction: an interactive prompt walk
through the same registry that builds a ready-to-paste front-matter
block, copying it to the clipboard (via the optional `clipr` package) or
printing it if no clipboard is available.

```r
quartifyr::header_helper("report")   # or "memo"
```

It's meant as a starting point for a new project, not a full editor --
richer constructs like `synopsis:`'s multi-line/embedded-figure values
(see `vignette("quarto-extension")`'s "Synopsis" section) are left for
hand-editing afterward. Check the result with `validate_header()`.

## A load-bearing detail: working directory

`reportifyr`/`pyro` locate their Python venv and project config by
walking **up from R's current working directory** looking for a
`.*_init.json` marker; they ignore path arguments for this.
`render_report()` derives the actual project root from `shell_qmd` and
wraps every `reportifyr::` call in `withr::with_dir(project_dir, ...)`,
so it's safe to call from an R session rooted anywhere. Calling
`reportifyr` functions directly without that scoping, from an R session
whose working directory isn't the target project, has been observed to
silently resolve the *wrong* project and seed a stray
`pyproject.toml`/`.venv`/`.rpfy-logs/` wherever the session happened to
be.

**A stricter version of the same trap applies to `pyro` itself.**
`pyro::get_proj_dir()` (`getOption("venv_dir") %||% here::here()`)
caches its result for the life of an R session, independent of
`withr::with_dir()` -- confirmed directly: calling it from two different
`with_dir()`-scoped directories in the same session returns the
*first*-resolved directory both times. Rendering two different projects
in one R session can otherwise write the second project's Python
dependency group into the *first* project's `pyproject.toml`.
`render_report()`'s internal bridge (`.run_quartifyr_styling_cli()`)
works around this by setting `venv_dir` explicitly via
`withr::local_options()` rather than relying on `pyro`'s cwd-based
default; `initialize_quartifyr_project()` passes `venv_dir`/
`pyproject_dir` explicitly to `pyro::write_group_to_pyproject()`/
`pyro::initialize_python()` for the same reason. This only matters if
you're calling `pyro::` directly yourself -- `render_report()` and the
`styling_*()`/`initialize_quartifyr_project()` functions already handle
it.

## Word field recalculation (optional, off by default)

Quarto/pandoc docx output contains native Word field codes (`TOC`,
`SEQ`, `REF`) that don't self-populate. For anyone opening the delivered
docx in real Microsoft Word, this is already handled for free: the
reference-doc sets `<w:updateFields w:val="true"/>`, which tells Word to
recalculate every field automatically on open. This doesn't help a
headless pipeline or LibreOffice running non-interactively; see
`vignette("styling")`'s `recalculate-fields` section for the
experimental step that covers that case, and its known reliability
caveat.

Known coverage gap even when it *does* work: LibreOffice only recognizes
the main document ToC as an updatable index. `quarto-plus`'s List of
Figures/List of Tables and plain `REF`-style cross-references aren't
recalculated by this step and still need a manual Word update.
